question: During indigestion, the stomach produces too much acid, that may be neutralised by which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnesium hydroxide (Milk of magnesia)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Indigestion** occurs when the stomach produces excess acid, leading to discomfort and symptoms like heartburn or bloating.
 
• **Magnesium hydroxide**, commonly known as **Milk of magnesia**, is an **antacid** that neutralizes stomach acid. It reacts with excess acid to form water and magnesium chloride, thereby reducing acidity.
 
• **Milk of magnesia** is widely used as a remedy for **acid indigestion**, heartburn, and upset stomachs due to its ability to **reduce gastric acidity.**
 
• Magnesium hydroxide also has a mild laxative effect, which can help relieve constipation, a condition often accompanying indigestion.
 
• Other compounds such as magnesium sulfate, magnesium oxide, and magnesium carbonate do not serve as effective antacids like magnesium hydroxide. They have different uses and do not neutralize stomach acid efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnesium hydroxide (Milk of magnesia):**

 
 
• It is a chemical compound with the formula Mg(OH)₂.
 
• When dissolved in water, it dissociates into **magnesium ions (Mg²⁺)** and **hydroxide ions (OH⁻)**, which neutralize stomach acid.
 
• Commonly used for **relieving indigestion**, heartburn, and mild constipation.
 
• The dosage of milk of magnesia should be taken as directed, as excessive use may lead to diarrhea due to its laxative properties.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium sulfate:**
 
 
• Also known as Epsom salt, it is primarily used for **relieving muscle pain** and as a laxative, but it is not effective as an antacid.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium oxide:**
 
 
• It is used as a dietary supplement for **magnesium deficiency** and sometimes as a mild laxative, but it is less effective in neutralizing stomach acid compared to magnesium hydroxide.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium carbonate:**
 
 
• Although it has mild antacid properties, it is not as effective as magnesium hydroxide (Milk of magnesia) for treating acid indigestion.
 
 
 
• **Antacid Mechanism:**
 
 
• Antacids work by neutralizing hydrochloric acid (HCl) in the stomach, leading to the formation of a salt and water, thereby reducing acidity and providing relief from symptoms of indigestion.
 
• For instance, the reaction of magnesium hydroxide with stomach acid can be represented as:

 **Mg(OH)₂ + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + 2H₂O**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Acid indigestion:** Caused by overproduction of hydrochloric acid in the stomach, leading to discomfort and symptoms like burning sensation in the chest or bloating.
 
• **Neutralization reaction:** The process by which an antacid reacts with stomach acid to reduce acidity.
 
• **Usage caution:** Overuse of antacids, including milk of magnesia, may lead to side effects such as diarrhea or electrolyte imbalances.
 
• **Consultation:** Always consult a healthcare professional for proper dosage and usage of antacids, especially for prolonged symptoms of indigestion.
